answer.rationale: Competitor price cut has created immediate churn risk in price-sensitive SMB segment. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for SMB acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_57 shows referral incentives work well but primarily for established customers—less relevant to immediate retention crisis. Onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31) and activation messaging (memory_91) drive adoption of new users but do not directly address churn of existing price-sensitive accounts now evaluating alternatives. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to SMB churn pressure. Promotional pricing is the only lever directly calibrated to price-sensitive segment retention. Small guarded test preserves optionality: we can learn effectiveness on at-risk cohort without broad margin dilution. We flag downstream risk because aggressive pricing may reset customer willingness-to-pay and create long-term margin compression. We preserve uncertainty by keeping test scope narrow and committing to post-test analysis before rollout.
